To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the most important predictor of breast cancer prognosis, the presence of lymph node metastasis, is associated with a unique set of gene expression changes that are involved in extracellular matrix degradation, cell proliferation and survival.

a set of 51 genes is differentially expressed between primary and lymph node metastatic breast tumors and the genes are involved in extracellular matrix remodeling, transcription, signal transductions, and immune response.

we have identified a unique set of gene expression signatures that are differentially expressed between primary breast tumors and their corresponding lymph node metastases and these signatures may provide insight into the molecular events that are required for successful lymphatic colonization.

understanding the mechanisms of tumor metastasis.
the molecular mechanisms that allow tumor cells to disseminate and colonize distant tissues.
the development of novel diagnostic and therapeutic approaches for breast cancer metastasis.

a gene expression signature that distinguishes between primary breast cancer and lymph node metastasis was identified.
a gene expression signature has been defined which is associated with breast cancer lymph node metastases.
a gene expression signature that can define breast cancer metastases has been found and that this gene expression signature is associated with the metastatic potential of breast cancer cells.
